artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan pairing both endpoints of every directory move in /todo's two recipe copies, naming the invariant in git-staging-scope.md, and adding a behavioral-plus-static regression suite.

memory_candidates.content: Migrating a git commit pathspec from a bare directory token to an explicit file list has a specific, predictable blind spot: a directory token covers BOTH endpoints of every rename inside it incidentally, while an explicit list covers only what it names. If the accumulator built during such a migration is only ever taught to collect each move's DESTINATION, every vacated source's removal is left unstaged -- the copy lands as a fresh `create mode`, the old tree stays in the index pointing at files that no longer exist, and the commit still exits 0 reporting success. No pathspec lint can catch this: a lint classifies only tokens that are PRESENT, and an omission is not a textual pattern. Likewise, a commit wrapper's own pathspec-classification gates only ever inspect pathspecs they are GIVEN. Practical rule: any `mv` whose two endpoints are both inside the staged tree must contribute BOTH endpoints to the pathspec list, explicitly and together, in the same commit. When auditing such a migration, enumerate every call site that performs a rename AND builds a commit pathspec -- those are exactly the sites the migration silently narrowed.
